chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Fizari al-Kufi. He said: Ja'far ibn Sahl narrated to us from Sa'id ibn Muhammad from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa. He said: Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) said to me:
Surely, the family of a man are like his prisoners. Whoever is blessed by Allah with a favor, let him be generous to his dependents. If he does not, that blessing is about to be removed from him.

key_terms.اسراء: Prisoners — captives, used metaphorically for dependents
key_terms.عيال: Family / dependents — those who rely on a man's provision
key_terms.نعمة: Blessing — a divine favor or bounty

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Musa al-Kadhim say about providing for one's family?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) teaches that a man's family members are like his prisoners of war, entirely dependent on his care. Whoever receives a divine blessing should share it generously with his dependents, for failure to do so risks the removal of that blessing. This teaching from the assembly of 368 AH reflects the Islamic obligation to provide for one's family with gratitude.
word_analysis: is about to / it is feared

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-`Attar narrated to us from Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Malik al-Fizari al-Kufi. He said: Ja`far b. Sahl narrated to us from Sa`id b. Muhammad from Mas`ada b. Sadaqa. He said: Abu’l Hasan Musa b. Ja`far (as) said:

Surely, the family of a man are [like] his prisoners. Whoever is given a blessing by Allah should give ease to his prisoners. Whoever does not do that or doubts [this], that blessing will be removed from him.
